name: sol_defi_as_12
description: Missing caller validation in AMM/swap callback functions
question: The source file in `source` defines a callback function (such as a swap/flash callback invoked by a pool or router) that trusts msg.sender-supplied data or performs token transfers/state updates without verifying that msg.sender is the legitimate pool/factory-authorized contract that initiated the callback, allowing an attacker to call the callback directly or via a malicious contract to manipulate balances or steal funds; this excludes callbacks that check msg.sender against a stored pool address, factory-derived address, or authorized caller list before acting.
criteria: A uniswapV3SwapCallback or similar swap callback transfers tokens based on amounts passed in calldata without checking msg.sender equals the expected pool address
A flashLoan or flash callback function executes arbitrary logic or moves funds using a 'data' parameter without verifying the caller is the authorized lending pool/factory
A callback function reads self-reported token addresses or amounts from calldata and performs transferFrom/transfer without validating msg.sender against a factory-computed pool address
A receive/onTokenTransfer style hook updates internal accounting or state based on caller-supplied parameters with no require(msg.sender == pool) or equivalent authorization check
